question_text: A railway employee is waving a white-red-white flag at a level crossing. What does this mean?

options.text: You must wait in front of the level crossing
You may cross the rails carefully
The flag is only meant for the train driver

correct_answers.text: You must wait in front of the level crossing

comment: If a railroad employee waves a white-red-white flag in front of a railroad crossing, you must wait at a safe distance before the crossing. Waving the flag means that the railroad crossing is blocked until the train has passed and the railroad employee stops the blockage.

question_text: When must you wait at a level crossing?

options.text: When a flashing red light comes on
When the barriers are being lowered
When a railway employee is waving a white-red-white flag

correct_answers.text: When a flashing red light comes on
When the barriers are being lowered
When a railway employee is waving a white-red-white flag

comment: All road users are required to stop and wait immediately before a level crossing in the following situations: when the signal system's red flashing light comes on, when the barriers start to lower, when the barriers are closed, when a staff member waves a white-red-white flag , You must wait until the blockage is released again.

question_text: You are approaching a level crossing with half barriers and flashing lights. The red light is flashing but the barrier is still open. What do you do?

options.text: Wait in front of the St. Andrew's Cross
Proceed as long as the half barrier is open
If no rail vehicle is in sight, cross the level crossing

correct_answers.text: Wait in front of the St. Andrew's Cross

comment: When the red flashing light of a barrier system lights up before rail traffic, all road users must stop in front of the diagonal cross. Driving on is strictly prohibited even if the half barrier is still open. The barriers have fast closing times and can jam vehicles. Rail vehicles are approaching at high speeds and have a very long braking distance of several hundred meters. Therefore, they cannot react situationally to obstacles.

question_text: A railway employee is waving a red lamp at a level crossing. What does this mean?

options.text: You must wait in front of the level crossing
You may cross the rails carefully
The red lamp is of no significance for you

correct_answers.text: You must wait in front of the level crossing

comment: All car drivers and other road users must wait at a safe distance before the crossing if a member of the railway staff secures a low-traffic level crossing with a red light. Waving the red light means that the tracks are inaccessible and trains have priority.

question_text: You are approaching a level crossing where the barriers are open. What do you do?

options.text: Approach at moderate speed, look along the railway line
Wait in front of the level crossing if you would have to wait on it because of traffic congestion
Proceed at the same speed as road traffic always has precedence in such cases

correct_answers.text: Approach at moderate speed, look along the railway line
Wait in front of the level crossing if you would have to wait on it because of traffic congestion

comment: Nevertheless, as you approach a railroad crossing with the barriers open, you must reduce speed and be aware of the track. The car driver should make sure that the transition is possible without danger and that no rail vehicle is approaching. When you see that a traffic jam could occur, it is necessary to keep a distance so that no car will end up standing on the rails. Rail transport always has priority.

question_text: At the entrance to an industrial estate, there is a St. Andrew's Cross with the supplementary sign "Industrial estate, rail vehicles have precedence". What must you remember?

options.text: Approach level crossings at moderate speed only
Rail vehicles have precedence at all level crossings
Motor vehicles have precedence at level crossings without St. Andrew's Cross

correct_answers.text: Approach level crossings at moderate speed only
Rail vehicles have precedence at all level crossings

comment: Even if there are no barriers and no diagonal crosses at the level crossings in the entire industrial area, motor vehicle drivers must give priority to all rail vehicles. Always expect a train to come, observe the railway lines accurately and approach the tracks only with moderate speed.

question_text: These level crossing barriers have not moved for some time now. What is the right course of action?

options.text: I do not cross the level crossing
I report the fault to the police
I cross the level crossing taking extra care

correct_answers.text: I do not cross the level crossing
I report the fault to the police

comment:
Apparently there is a fault with the railway barrier. It is therefore not safe to use the railway crossing. Do not cross the railway crossing under any circumstances; if a train is approaching, there is an acute danger to your life and there is also a risk that you will not be able to get through under the barriers and get stuck.
Inform the police about the fault at the railway crossing so that the problem can be fixed.

question_text: You are driving along a forest track and approach a level crossing without St. Andrew's Cross. What do you do?

options.text: Proceed at moderate speed and check to see if a rail vehicle is approaching
Listen out in case a rail vehicle signals its approach by whistling or ringing a bell
Proceed without taking any special precautions since rail vehicles are required to wait here

correct_answers.text: Proceed at moderate speed and check to see if a rail vehicle is approaching
Listen out in case a rail vehicle signals its approach by whistling or ringing a bell

comment: Even without the diagonal cross, a car driver must always give priority to a rail vehicle on field and forest paths. Approach the railroad crossing at moderate speed and listen for a train approaching. Observe the track and stop, if necessary, to let the rail vehicle pass.

question_text: What do you do at a level crossing when the barriers are closed?

options.text: Wait before the St. Andrew's Cross without obstructing junctions
If possible, switch on the side lights when it is dark
Use the road area and wait directly in front of the barrier

correct_answers.text: Wait before the St. Andrew's Cross without obstructing junctions
If possible, switch on the side lights when it is dark

comment: At a level crossing with closed gates, all car drivers have to wait in front of the diagonal cross. If there is no traffic sign, a safe distance to the rails must be observed. Be careful not to block intersections or T-junctions when waiting. In the dark, lighting must be switched on, parking light is sufficient.

question_text: When are you allowed to cross a level crossing with flashing lights but no barriers after a train has passed?

options.text: When the flashing red light goes out
Immediately after the train has passed, even if the flashing red light is still on
As soon as the oncoming traffic sets off, even if the flashing red light is still on

correct_answers.text: When the flashing red light goes out

comment: You may only cross the level crossing after the red flashing light turns off, as another train could follow. Do not be fooled by oncoming traffic to drive on if the car driver waiting on the opposite site already starts driving too early after the train has passed through.

question_text: You are approaching a level crossing with barriers. Where must you wait if you would have to stop on the rails in case of traffic congestion?

options.text: In front of the St. Andrew's Cross
Just before the rails
Level with the barrier

correct_answers.text: In front of the St. Andrew's Cross

comment: If you are unable to pass the railroad crossing quickly due to slow traffic, then stop in front of the diagonal cross. Waiting directly in front of the rails or at the level of the barriers is prohibited, because at these positions you may be hit by the dynamic pressure of the train, by the train itself or trapped by the barriers.

question_text: What do you do here?

options.text: Approach at moderate speed and wait
Proceed as the roadway is only blocked for oncoming traffic

correct_answers.text: Approach at moderate speed and wait

comment: All car drivers and other road users must wait at a safe distance if railway staff guards a low-traffic level crossing with a white-red-white flag. Under no circumstances should you cross the tracks here, as the transition is blocked by the swinging of the flag and trains have priority.

question_text: The barrier of a level crossing inside a built-up area is closed. Where must you wait?

options.text: In front of the St. Andrew's Cross
Before the last beacon
Before the first beacon

correct_answers.text: In front of the St. Andrew's Cross

comment: Trucks and vehicles with trailers (vehicles over 7.5 t permissible total mass) are only required to wait outside of built-up areas behind the level crossing (80 m) ahead marker. Inside a built-up area they have to wait in front of the diagonal crosses.

question_text: What does this traffic sign mean?

options.text: Indication of existing overhead electrical wires
Rail traffic always has priority
You must always wait when a rail vehicle is approaching

correct_answers.text: Indication of existing overhead electrical wires
Rail traffic always has priority
You must always wait when a rail vehicle is approaching

comment: The diagonal crosses indicate that rail transport has priority here. As a car driver you need to wait when a rail vehicle is approaching. A lightning bolt in the diagonal cross is an indication of an electrical overhead line, which is important for special transports with a big height.

question_text: A light signal with no level crossing sign is positioned before a level crossing, and in front of a junction with a road to the right. The red light is illuminated. Where must you wait?

options.text: At the stop line
In front of the light signal, if there is no stop line
I can drive up to the level crossing after watching out for other traffic

correct_answers.text: At the stop line
In front of the light signal, if there is no stop line

comment: In the event of a red light, the car driver must stop in any case. In order not to block the traffic from the road going to the right, the red light is located several meters from the actual railroad crossing. Wait at the stop line or at the light sign if no line is available.

question_text: What must you do in this situation?

options.text: - stop in front of the level crossing
- drive on past to the left of the flagman
- drive on past to the right of the flagman

correct_answers.text: - stop in front of the level crossing

comment: The railway employee secures the level crossing and therefore you should stop before the St. Andrew's cross.

question_text: Who is required to stop at a level crossing with a red flashing light in the form of an arrow point to the right?

options.text: Traffic turning right
Traffic moving straight ahead
Traffic turning left

correct_answers.text: Traffic turning right

comment: A diagonal cross with a red flashing light in the form of an arrow to the right can be found behind an intersection or T-junction after a railroad crossing. The right arrow indicates that the car drivers who turn right must wait.

question_text: What does this traffic sign combination indicate?

options.text: - which I may approach at a maximum speed of 10 km/h
- which I may cross at a maximum speed of 10 km/h
- over which rail traffic may pass at a maximum speed of 10 km/h

correct_answers.text: - which I may approach at a maximum speed of 10 km/h
- which I may cross at a maximum speed of 10 km/h

comment: The traffic sign combination shows you a level crossing. The car driver may approach the level crossing only at 10 km/h and cross it at that speed.

question_text: What is the right course of action now?

options.text: I wait in front of the level crossing
I carefully cross the tracks
I wait at the tracks

correct_answers.text: I wait in front of the level crossing

comment: If there is a risk that you might come to a stop on the rails due to a traffic jam situation or stagnant traffic, stop in front of the diagonal cross and wait until you can safely and quickly cross the level crossing. Fatal accidents occur when a car standing on the rails cannot avoid the approaching train.

question_text: You are approaching a rail crossing. The barrier begins to lower. What should you do?

options.text: I wait in front of the level crossing
I continue driving if there is no train in sight
I switch on my hazard lights

correct_answers.text: I wait in front of the level crossing

comment: When a driver approaches a gate that lowers, he/she must wait in front of the level crossing. This also applies if no rail vehicle is yet to be seen. Switching on the hazard light is not required.

question_text: Where do you have to anticipate encountering rail crossings with no technical safeguards?

options.text: On less-frequently used roads
In industrial zones and port areas
On dirt tracks and forest tracks

correct_answers.text: On less-frequently used roads
In industrial zones and port areas
On dirt tracks and forest tracks

comment: In industrial and port areas, on field and forest paths, as well as on roads with little traffic, you should expect a railway crossing without a barrier or traffic light (technically unprotected).

question_text: You want to cross a level crossing with the barriers open. What is correct?

options.text: I have to approach the level crossing at a moderate speed
I expect there to be bumps in the road when crossing the level crossing
I am only allowed to cross the tracks at walking speed

correct_answers.text: I have to approach the level crossing at a moderate speed
I expect there to be bumps in the road when crossing the level crossing

comment: Even when the barriers are open, you must always approach level crossings with caution and at a moderate speed. This gives you enough time to react to possible bumps and dangerous situations. Moderate speed in this context does not mean walking speed, because you can also drive faster than walking speed. In this way you can prevent possible dangerous situations with approaching trains or lowering barriers.

question_text: What should you do now?

options.text: - stop before the cross
- cross the level crossing quickly
- drive through an open barrier

correct_answers.text: - stop before the cross

comment: Level crossings may not be crossed when the flashing lights above the St. Andrew's Cross are on or the barriers are lowered.
